title: Wikipedia (screen content)
subtitle: yah265 against x265 at the same file size

notes.heading: How this was made
body: Screen content: a 4.3-second recording of a browser scrolling Wikipedia, 1920x1080 at 30 fps. It's the whole clip, 130 frames.
This page shows screen content on purpose. yah265 detects screen frames and searches their scroll motion, so its lead here is much larger than on camera footage.
The source is Wikipedia_1920x1080p30.y4m from the AOM CTC screen-content set (8-bit 4:2:0), copied to a lossless intermediate.

Both encoders ran through ffmpeg at preset medium under CRF, with default threads and no tune. yah265 ran at CRF 24, about 1.2 Mbit/s. x265's CRF was then solved in steps of 0.1 until its MP4 came within 2% of yah265's size. CRF 38.0 lands at 101.0% of the size.
Each encode is scored against the lossless source with VMAF v1, model vmaf_v1.0.16_3d0h, on every frame. No reference stream is hosted here, to keep the page small.
Wikipedia screen recording by Thomas Daede, released under CC0 1.0. The page shown is Wikipedia's, whose text is available under CC BY-SA 4.0.

commands.label: yah265
commands.text: ffmpeg -i source_1920x1080.mkv -an -c:v libyah265 -preset medium -crf 24 -tag:v hvc1 -movflags +faststart yah265.mp4

commands.label: x265
commands.text: ffmpeg -i source_1920x1080.mkv -an -c:v libx265 -preset medium -crf 38.0 -x265-params log-level=error -tag:v hvc1 -movflags +faststart x265.mp4

commands.label: Scoring
commands.text: ffmpeg -i <source|encode> -pix_fmt yuv420p10le -strict -1 -f yuv4mpegpipe <fifo>; vmaf -q -r ref.fifo -d dis.fifo --model path=vmaf_v1.0.16_3d0h.json:name=v1:cambi.enc_bitdepth=8:cambi.enc_width=1920:cambi.enc_height=1080 --json -o <out>
